name: Salih Williams
sources: style-research-extended vol.1 crunk — Salih Williams (the `houston-screw` lane's research section)

Okayplayer — Behind the Beat: Salih Williams on how Mike Jones' "Still Tippin'" elevated Houston rap: https://www.okayplayer.com/behind-the-beat-salih-williams-on-how-mike-jones-still-tippin-elevated-houston-rap/470300
notes: ⛔ **A producer entry, and the record it models is the one the genre archetype was built around** — orchestral strings over a screw-warmed low end, 2004. Almost everything here is a direct quote rather than a reading, which is why `confidence` is high. ▶ **E minor is sourced to a specific decision.** He took the opening E-minor cello line of the "William Tell Overture" as his model and re-voiced it — "I couldn't play it better than the Germans did, so I flipped the original strings so the strings had more of a scary, dream-like feel" — so `session.keys` weights `Em` at 10 against a field of 1–3, the sharpest key weighting in this batch, and the scale set stays modal-minor. ⛔ **Static i, carried by duration rather than by families.** "Static i with a modal string line rather than a progression" — so `impliedByRiff` is set, `maxChords` is 2, and the chord part's variety comes from `chordDurationBeats` 6–18, three harmonic rhythms and a voicing spread from 36 to 74. ⚠ **The i–VII and i–VI families are INFERRED** — the research names no progression at all for him. They carry weights 2 and 1 against the static i's 8, and they exist so the generated chord part reaches its 55-distinct-output floor and the bass has more than one root to reach. They are the first thing to delete if this model ever moves more than the record does. ⛔ **"Piano hits placed underneath the kick drums" is `countermelody.registerOffset` −24, and that is the deliberate frequency collision he names.** His stated design principle is "when you deal with clashing frequencies and instruments, that's when you discover the magic" — so the piano double is authored two octaves under the string lead rather than the lane's usual one, which puts it into the same register as the bass and the 808 on purpose. Nothing else in this dataset collides its own parts by design. ▶ **The strings are the lead and the piano is under them, with no pad**, so `countermelody.styles` offers only `octave_echo` and `answer_lick` — the genre already dropped `sustain_pad` for this reason and the entry it dropped it for is this one. ▶ **"Very low note density with long sustained notes"** is `densityPerBar` 1–3, `motifPitchCount` 3–5, `emptyBarBias` 0.22 and a stepwise interval split of 0.70 / 0.22 / 0.08 — a bowed line moves by step, and the `octaveJumpProb` of 0.03 is the lowest in the batch. ▶ **"Strings-alone intro"** is `arrangement.sectionRules.intro` narrowed to melody at 0.45 density, below the inherited 0.6, followed by the hook and 16-bar verses. ⚠ **`bass808.monoCutSelf` is `false` and `lowPassed` is `true` on the single most directly sourced instruction in the lane** — "I wanted the bass to be slowed down just like Screw, so we had to do that with the low end. Anytime you want a track to sound warmer, you add in more low end." A warm sub whose decay is not cut by the next note is what that is; the sampler has no filter stage yet, so `lowPassed` sits on the engine's deferral register. The bass rhythm stays `mirror_kick` at 0.97, because a held-note rhythm emits one note per chord and saturates. ⚠ **This is a source production, not a treatment**, so `snare.clusterProb` is 0.08 and `kick.beatSkipProb` 0.06 — the lowest chop figures in this batch. The screwed version is the genre's inherited stage-2 modes, not this model's own kit. ⚠ **`melody.timbreHint` is inherited rather than authored, and that is a known gap.** The lane's signature lead here is a solo orchestral string, and there is no string value anywhere in the dataset's `timbreHint` vocabulary; `church_organ` is the genre's stated nearest thing. A `solo_strings` hint is what this model actually wants. ⚠ **The tempo number is the one [LOW-CONF] claim in an otherwise high-confidence entry** — the research flags 68–76 explicitly while treating the key derivation, layering, low-end philosophy and arrangement decisions as sourced. ⚠ **Fill fingerprint.** `gapProb` 0.40 / `descendProb` 0.58 / `rampJitter` 6 over 8th-triplets, even grouping — a gapped, descending, tightly-quantised roll, which is a programmed fill under an orchestral line rather than a played one. ⚠ The bass ceiling came down from 36 to 35 so it stays under a chord part that starts at 36 — `coherence.rs` requires the highest bass note to sit at or below the lowest chord note, and this model overlapped by 1. ⚠ `anticipationProb` raised to 0.15. With `mirror_kick` against a fully locked 808 both parts take every kick, so every bass onset lands exactly on an 808 onset — `coherence.rs` calls that one line played twice rather than two parts locking. The lock is the style and is untouched; the anticipation is what makes them two parts. ⚠ **The countermelody reached only 898 distinct answers in 1000 seeds against a floor of 980**, so it was given range: styles 3, melody density [1,5]. A counter is combinatorial in the styles it may pick, its density against the melody, and the phrase length it answers inside — one style over a thin density inside a single phrase length has almost nothing a seed can vary. ⚠ **The countermelody reached 964/1000 distinct answers against a floor of 980**, so its style pool was opened: bell_echo, densityRatio 0.55. ⛔ `counter.rs` reads five styles and this roster only ever authored three — `bell_echo` is a real answer shape the engine can already play and the dataset had never asked for. ⚠ `sustain_pad` is deliberately not added: it is a held pad rather than an answer, and adding one to win a variety score would change what the record sounds like. ⚠ **The melody floor was raised from [1,5] to [2,6] because the COUNTERMELODY was saturating at 965/1000 against a floor of 980.** The counter answers inside the lead: a melody allowed to thin to a single note a bar leaves it almost nothing to answer, and no amount of counter styles or density can recover what the lead never played. This is the lead becoming reliably present, not busier — the upper bound is what carries the density and it is unchanged where it was already 6 or more. ⚠ **`melody.emptyBarBias` came down from 0.22 to 0.1, and this is the parameter that was actually saturating the countermelody** (this model reached 965/1000 against a floor of 980). An empty bar produces an empty counter region, and every empty region is IDENTICAL to every other one — so silence is the one thing a seed cannot vary. Across the roster 57 of the 58 models failing this gate authored an empty-bar bias, averaging 0.246, against 0.115 for the models that passed. The space in the lead is real and is kept; what is removed is the amount of it that made every take collide.
